title: Feature/1960
summary: Since the last plan, a game needs **at least 3 hints** again (and at least 3 chances). Starting a round now **closes the panel**, so the round runs in a restyled bar over the reader. **End game** and **Back to main menu** in that bar reopen the panel. Editing a game has a **Save & Start** button, and **Set as target** is hidden during a round. On a phone, the bar sits above the bottom bars instead of being cut off, and winning reopens the panel. Overall the PR adds **Find the Verse**, a new extension with a guessing game: someone creates a game by picking a secret verse and writing hints, then a player taps verses in the reader to guess, and the game says whether the secret verse is earlier or later. Games can be saved to your account to play, edit, or delete later.

links.label: Issue 1960: Port the "find this verse" game for the Bible stack

setup.title: Open the preview build
setup.body: Use the button above, in Chrome, Edge, Firefox or Safari on a computer (one section later uses a phone). If the page shows an error or doesn't load, the build may still be deploying: wait a few minutes and reload. If it looks like the old version, do a hard refresh (Ctrl+Shift+R on Windows, Cmd+Shift+R on Mac).

setup.title: Sign in
setup.body: Games are saved to your account, so most tests need you signed in. Open **Settings** (the gear icon), choose to sign in, enter your email address, then type the code that arrives in your inbox. Use an inbox you can check.

setup.title: Install the Find the Verse extension
setup.body: Open the app's menu and go to **Extensions**. If **Find the Verse** isn't already under **Installed**, install it from **Available**. If you can't find **Find the Verse** at all, mark every test **Blocked** and say so in the note.

setup.title: Find the game button
setup.body: A new **Find the Verse** button (a crosshair / target icon) appears in the app's toolbar. If you don't see it, look in the toolbar's overflow (**...**) menu. Clicking it opens the game panel at the side of the screen. In these tests, "the panel" means that game panel, and "the bar" means the small floating game bar that appears over the reader during a round.

setup.title: Start with no saved games
setup.body: If you tested an earlier plan for this PR with the same account, your old games will still be listed. Delete them first (on each card, **...** → **Delete** → **Delete**), so the lists match what the tests describe.

setup.title: Use one English translation
setup.body: Read in an English translation such as **BSB** for every test, so the book names and verse text match what's written here.

sections.title: Creating a game
sections.intro: Make the game the later sections play: secret verse **John 3:16**, four chances.

tests.title: The panel starts with a Create a game button
steps: Click the **Find the Verse** toolbar button.
expected: A panel titled **Find the Verse** opens with a 🔍 icon, a short description of the game, and a **Create a game** button.
No **My saved games** list is shown yet (you haven't saved any).

tests.title: Saving an empty game shows one problem at a time
tests.why: The form checks the name first, then the secret verse, then the hints, and scrolls to whichever is wrong. The hint check is covered in its own test below.
steps: Click **Create a game**.
Without filling anything in, click **Save game** (the second of the two buttons at the bottom; the first is **Start game**).
Type `Test game` in **Game name** and click **Save game** again.
expected: After the first click, a red message **Give this game a name.** appears under the name box.
After the second click, the name message goes away and **Pick the secret verse before saving.** appears under **Secret verse** instead.
No game is saved and the panel stays on the **Create a game** form.

tests.title: Typing a reference picks the secret verse and opens it in the reader
tests.before: Continue on the form from the previous test.
steps: In the box with the placeholder `e.g. John 1:1`, type `John 3:16-17` and click **Go**.
Replace it with `Hezekiah 1:1` and press **Enter**.
Replace it with `John 3:16` and click **Go**.
expected: `John 3:16-17` shows **Pick a single verse, like John 1:1, not a range.**
`Hezekiah 1:1` shows **Couldn't recognise that reference. Try “John 1:1”.**
`John 3:16` shows a grey box reading **John 3:16** with the verse text in italics ("For God so loved the world…"), and the reader jumps to John chapter 3.

tests.title: Select from reader lets you pick the verse by tapping it
tests.why: The second way to choose a secret verse.
tests.before: Continue on the form. John 3:16 is the current secret verse.
steps: Click **Select from reader…**.
In the reader, click verse **John 3:3**.
In the toolbar that appears for the verse, click **Set as target**.
Type `John 3:16` in the reference box and click **Go** again, so the secret verse is back to John 3:16 for the rest of the tests.
expected: After **Select from reader…**, a coloured box says **Tap any verse in the reader, then choose Set as target in the toolbar.** with a **Cancel** button.
The verse toolbar shows a **Set as target** button (with a pin icon) alongside its usual buttons.
After **Set as target**, the coloured box goes away and the preview shows **John 3:3** with its text.
After the last step the preview shows **John 3:16** again.

tests.title: At least 3 hints are needed, and you can add or remove chances
tests.why: Failed on the plan for commit `53bbd66`: "game can be saved with empty chances". Changed since commit `9ea551a`: hints were fully optional there; now at least 3 must be filled in, and you can't go below 3 chances.
tests.before: Continue on the form (name `Test game`, secret verse John 3:16).
steps: Look at the **Chances** section.
Click the red **×** next to rows 5, 6 and 7 until only four rows are left.
Click **+ Add chance**, then click **×** on the new row.
Fill in hint boxes 1 and 2 only: `New Testament` and `One of the Gospels`. Click **Save game**.
Now fill in box 4: type `A very famous verse`, press Enter once, and type `second line`. Leave box 3 empty.
expected: At first there are seven empty hint rows, each with the grey placeholder **Hint…**, and the label reads **Chances (7)**. The line under it says **Start with 7. You can add more or remove down to 3. At least 3 hints are needed.**
The label counts down as rows are removed, ending at **Chances (4)**; **+ Add chance** makes it 5, and removing that row brings it back to 4.
With only two hints filled in, **Save game** shows the red message **At least 3 hints are needed.** under the chances, and nothing is saved.
As soon as box 4 is filled in, the red message goes away. Box 4 grows to show both lines of text.
You'll check that you can't go below 3 rows in a later test.

tests.title: Saving the game adds it to My saved games, and it survives a reload
tests.before: The form has name `Test game`, secret verse John 3:16, and four chances (hints in boxes 1, 2 and 4; box 3 empty).
steps: Click **Save game**.
Look at the card under **My saved games**.
Click **Show reference** on the card.
Reload the page, then open the panel again from the toolbar button.
expected: The panel goes back to the start screen, and a **My saved games** list shows one card: **Test game**, a **Show reference** link, and **Saved game · 4 chances · <today's date>**, with a **Play** button and a **...** menu.
The reference is hidden until you click **Show reference**, which replaces the name with **John 3:16**.
After the reload the card is still there.

tests.title: Cancel throws a draft away without saving
steps: Click **Create a game**.
Type `Throwaway` as the name, then click **Cancel**.
Click **Create a game** again.
expected: **Cancel** returns to the start screen and no **Throwaway** card appears.
The new form is blank: empty name, no secret verse, seven empty hints.

tests.title: Start game plays straight from the form, without saving
tests.why: Changed since commit `9ea551a`: Start game now also needs 3 hints, and it closes the panel so the round runs in the bar over the reader. Before, the panel stayed open.
tests.before: Continue on the blank form from the previous test.
steps: Click **Start game** without filling anything in.
Type `Quick round` as the name and click **Start game** again.
Type `Psalm 23:1` in the reference box, click **Go**, and click **Start game** again.
Click **×** on rows until no **×** is left.
Fill in all the remaining hints: `Old Testament`, `Poetry`, `A shepherd`. Click **Start game**.
Click verse **Genesis 1:1** in the reader.
Click **End game** in the bar.
expected: With nothing filled in, **Give this game a name.** appears and no round starts. With only a name, **Pick the secret verse before saving.** appears instead. With a name and verse but no hints, **At least 3 hints are needed.** appears.
The **×** buttons disappear once there are three rows left (**Chances (3)**).

**Start game** closes the panel, the reader jumps to **Genesis 1**, and a bar appears near the bottom of the reader showing **Quick round**, **3 / 3 left**, a round **?** button, and an **End game** button.
After the guess, the bar shows **2 / 3 left** and **The verse is later in the Bible — try a book further along.**
**End game** removes the bar and opens the panel again on the start screen. Only **Test game** is under **My saved games**; no **Quick round** card was saved.

tests.title: Set as target on any verse starts a new game with that verse
tests.why: Issue 1960 asks for a way to start a game from the verse toolbar.
tests.before: The panel is on the start screen (no round in progress). Close the panel.
steps: Open **Romans 8** and click verse **Romans 8:28**.
In the verse toolbar, click **Set as target**.
Type `From toolbar` as the name.
Without leaving the form, click verse **Romans 8:1** in the reader and click **Set as target** again.
Click **Cancel**.
expected: The verse toolbar shows **Set as target** (pin icon) alongside its usual buttons, even though the game panel is closed.
Clicking it opens the panel on a fresh **Create a game** form with **Romans 8:28** and its text already filled in as the secret verse, an empty name, and seven empty chances.
The second **Set as target** changes the secret verse to **Romans 8:1** and keeps the name `From toolbar`.
**Cancel** returns to the start screen with no new card.

sections.title: Playing a game
sections.intro: Play `Test game` (secret verse John 3:16, four chances). Order matters: tests continue the same round until a test says to start a new one. Starting a round now closes the panel; the **Find the Verse** toolbar button reopens it at any time.

tests.title: Play closes the panel and starts a round at Genesis 1 in the bar
tests.why: Changed since commit `9ea551a`: the panel used to stay open after **Play**. It also covers the restyled bar.
steps: On the **Test game** card, click **Play**.
Click the round **?** button in the bar.
expected: The panel closes and the reader jumps to **Genesis 1**.

A bar near the bottom of the reader shows **Test game**, **4 / 4 left**, a **?** button, and an **End game** button. It has rounded corners and a thin border, like the reader's own toolbar, and **End game** looks like a button (with a border and background), not plain text.
Clicking **?** replaces it with the first hint: **New Testament**.

tests.title: A wrong book says later or earlier, greys out what's ruled out, and uses a chance
steps: Click verse **Genesis 1:1** in the reader.
Click **Genesis 1:1** again.
Open the book list (the book/chapter picker) and look at **Genesis**.
Click **?** in the bar to see the next hint.
expected: The normal verse toolbar does NOT appear when you click a verse; the click counts as a guess instead.
The bar says **The verse is later in the Bible — try a book further along.** and shows **3 / 4 left**.
Clicking the same verse again shows the same message but does NOT use another chance (still **3 / 4 left**).
The verses of Genesis 1 look faded, and **Genesis** is greyed out in the book list.
The **?** button is back (a new chance means a new hint) and shows **One of the Gospels**.

tests.title: Guessing past the verse says it's earlier, and the reveal buttons unlock in the panel at half the chances
tests.why: With four chances, the reveal buttons appear after two guesses (half, rounded up). They are only in the panel, not the bar.
steps: Use the book list to open **Revelation 1**.
Click verse **Revelation 1:1**.
Click the **Find the Verse** toolbar button to open the panel. Leave it open for the next tests.
expected: The bar says **The verse is earlier in the Bible — try a book further back.** and shows **2 / 4 left**.
**Revelation** is now greyed out in the book list, as well as Genesis.
There is no **?** button now, because chance 3 was saved without a hint.
When the panel opens, the bar disappears. The panel shows the same round: **Test game**, **2 / 4 left**, the last message, and two buttons, **Reveal hint** and **Reveal verse**.

tests.title: Right book and right chapter give their own messages, and the chapter list greys out ruled-out chapters
tests.before: The panel is open, in the middle of the round.
steps: Open **John 1** and click verse **John 1:1**.
Open the chapter list for John and look at chapter 1.
Open **John 3** and click verse **John 3:20**.
expected: After John 1:1: **Right book! The verse is in a later chapter.** and **1 / 4 left**. The **?** button is back and shows the two-line hint **A very famous verse** / **second line**. Chapter 1 is greyed out in John's chapter list.
After John 3:20: **Right chapter! The verse number is lower.** In John 3, verses 20 and after look faded.
The pill now reads **Out of chances** in red, with the message **You've used all your chances, but you can keep guessing — good luck!**

tests.title: Reveal hint blanks out about half the words of the verse
steps: Click **Reveal hint** in the panel.
expected: A box labelled **PARTIAL HINT** shows the verse with roughly half of its words replaced by `___`, in random places.
The **Reveal hint** button disappears; **Reveal verse** stays.

tests.title: Finding the verse shows the win screen, and Set as target stays hidden on it
tests.why: Changed since commit `9ea551a`: **Set as target** used to show on the win screen, and choosing it threw the result away. It's now hidden for the whole round.
steps: Click verse **John 3:16**.
Click verse **John 3:1** and look at the verse toolbar, if one appears.
Click **Back to main menu**.
Click a verse in the reader.
expected: Confetti falls, then 🎉 **You found it!**, **John 3:16**, the verse text in italics, and **5 guesses**.
Clicking another verse on the win screen does not show a **Set as target** button.
**Back to main menu** returns to the start screen with the **Test game** card.
The faded verses and greyed-out books and chapters are back to normal, and clicking a verse opens the normal verse toolbar, with **Set as target** back in it.

tests.title: Reveal verse shows the answer and dims the rest of the chapter
steps: Click **Play** on **Test game**.
Click **Genesis 1:1**, then open **Revelation 1** and click **Revelation 1:1**.
Click the **Find the Verse** toolbar button, then click **Reveal verse** in the panel.
Click another verse in the reader.
expected: **Play** closes the panel and the round starts fresh at **4 / 4 left** in the bar, with nothing greyed out from the last round.
**Reveal verse** opens **John 3**, scrolls to verse 16, and keeps it lit while the rest of the chapter is dimmed.
The panel shows **John 3:16** with the full verse text and **Better luck next time — keep going!**
Clicking another verse does not count as a guess and does not open the normal verse toolbar.

tests.title: End game in the panel stops the round
tests.before: Continue from the revealed round in the previous test, with the panel open.
steps: Click **End game** in the panel.
Click a verse in the reader.
expected: The panel returns to the start screen.
The dimmed verses return to normal, and clicking a verse opens the normal verse toolbar.

tests.title: End game and Back to main menu in the bar reopen the panel
tests.why: Changed since commit `9ea551a`: both buttons used to leave the panel closed, so you had to find the toolbar button again. The bar's win message is also new.
steps: Click **Play** on **Test game**.
Click verse **Genesis 1:1**, then click **End game** in the bar.
Click **Play** on **Test game** again. Open **John 3** and click verse **John 3:16**.
Click **Back to main menu** in the bar.
expected: **End game** removes the bar and the panel opens on the start screen.
After guessing John 3:16 with the panel closed, the bar shows **You found it!** next to a **Back to main menu** button.
**Back to main menu** removes the bar and opens the panel on the start screen, and clicking a verse opens the normal verse toolbar again.

tests.title: Edit changes the saved game instead of adding a copy
steps: On the **Test game** card, open the **...** menu and choose **Edit**.
Change the name to `Test game edited`, click **×** on row 3 (the empty one), and click **Save game**.
Reload the page and open the panel.
expected: The form title reads **Edit game**, with the name, the John 3:16 preview, and the four chances as you left them: hints 1, 2 and 4 filled in (4 still showing both lines) and 3 empty. The first button at the bottom reads **Save & Start** instead of **Start game**.
After removing row 3 there are three rows, all filled in, and no **×** buttons.
After saving there is still only one card: **Test game edited**, **3 chances**, with the original date.
It is still there after the reload.

tests.title: Save & Start saves your edits, then starts the round
tests.why: New since commit `9ea551a`. Before, starting from the edit form played the changes without saving them, so the saved copy kept the old hints.
steps: On **Test game edited**, open **...** and choose **Edit**.
Clear hint 2 (delete all its text) and click **Save & Start**.
Type `In the Gospels` in hint 2 and click **Save & Start** again.
Click verse **Genesis 1:1**, then click **?** in the bar.
Click **End game** in the bar. Open **...** → **Edit** on the card again, look at hint 2, then click **Cancel**.
expected: With only two hints filled in, **At least 3 hints are needed.** appears and no round starts.
With three hints, the panel closes and the round starts at **Genesis 1** with **3 / 3 left** in the bar.
After the guess, **?** shows **In the Gospels**.
When you edit the game again, hint 2 still reads **In the Gospels**: the change was saved. There is still only one card.

tests.title: Delete asks first, and Cancel keeps the game
steps: On the card, open **...** and choose **Delete**.
Click **Cancel**.
Open **...** again, choose **Delete**, then click **Delete**.
Reload the page and open the panel.
expected: The card shows **Delete this game?** with **Delete** and **Cancel** buttons in place of **Play**.
**Cancel** puts the card back as it was.
**Delete** removes the card, and the **My saved games** heading disappears with it.
After the reload the game is still gone.

tests.title: Saved games stay on your account and follow you to another browser
steps: Create and save a new game: name `Second browser`, secret verse `Psalm 23:1`, and three chances (remove rows down to three), each with a hint of your choice.
In a different browser (or a private/incognito window), open the preview, sign in with the same email, install **Find the Verse** if needed, and open the panel.
expected: The **Second browser** card appears there too, with **3 chances**.

tests.title: Saving in one browser doesn't erase a game saved in another
tests.why: Saving used to write back only this browser's copy of your list, silently deleting a game saved elsewhere in the meantime.
tests.before: Keep both browsers from the previous test open and signed in to the same account, with the panel open in both. Don't reload either one.
steps: In the first browser, create and save a game named `One` (any verse, three hints).
In the second browser, without reloading, create and save a game named `Two` (any verse, three hints).
Close and reopen the panel in each browser (don't reload).
expected: Both browsers list **One**, **Two** and **Second browser**. No game is missing.
Reopening the panel doesn't blank the list: the cards stay on screen while it refreshes.

tests.title: Deleting a game that was already deleted in another browser removes its card
tests.why: New since commit `9ea551a`. Before, the card stayed and pressing **Delete** seemed to do nothing.
tests.before: Both browsers from the previous test, panel open in both, showing **One**.
steps: In the first browser, delete **One** (**...** → **Delete** → **Delete**).
In the second browser, without reloading or reopening the panel, delete **One** the same way.
expected: In both browsers the **One** card disappears, with no error. **Two** and **Second browser** are still listed.

sections.title: Things that should not have changed

tests.title: The normal verse toolbar still works, with one extra button
tests.why: **Set as target** shows on every verse for anyone with the extension installed (except during a round), so check it doesn't get in the way.
steps: Click any verse, and use the toolbar to highlight it in a colour.
Click the verse again and remove the highlight.
Go to **Extensions**, uninstall **Find the Verse**, then click a verse.
expected: Highlighting and removing a highlight work as before. **Set as target** sits among the usual buttons without pushing any off the toolbar.
After uninstalling, **Set as target** is gone from the toolbar. Reinstall the extension if you have more tests to do.

sections.title: Signed out, phone, and dark mode

tests.title: Signed out, you can play a game but not save it
tests.before: Open the preview in a private/incognito window and don't sign in. Install **Find the Verse** from **Extensions** if it lets you; if it requires signing in, mark this test **Skip**.
steps: Open the panel and click **Create a game**.
Fill in the name `Guest game`, secret verse `John 1:1`, and the first three hints (any text).
Click **Sign in to save games**.
Click **Start game**, then click verse **Genesis 1:1**.
expected: No **My saved games** list is shown.
The buttons read **Start game** and **Sign in to save games**. Clicking **Sign in to save games** shows the red message **Sign in to save games** and nothing is saved.
**Start game** closes the panel, jumps to **Genesis 1**, and shows the bar with **7 / 7 left**; the guess says **The verse is later in the Bible — try a book further along.**

tests.title: On a phone, picking a secret verse works with the panel closed
tests.before: On a phone, signed in, with the extension installed.
steps: Open the panel, tap **Create a game**, then **Select from reader…**.
Close the panel.
Tap any verse, then tap **Set as target** in the verse toolbar.
Tap **Cancel** to throw the draft away.
expected: With the panel closed, a bar over the reader says **Tap any verse in the reader, then choose Set as target in the toolbar.** with a **Cancel** button. The whole bar is visible, not hidden behind the app's bottom bars.
After **Set as target** the panel reopens by itself and shows the verse you picked.

tests.title: On a phone, the game bar stays fully visible above the bottom bars
tests.why: Skipped on the plan for commit `53bbd66`: "(ui issue) the bar is cutoff in mobile". This commit moves the bar above the app's bottom bars and makes it follow them when they slide.
tests.before: On a phone, signed in, with the **Second browser** game saved (secret verse Psalm 23:1).
steps: Tap **Play** on **Second browser**.
Tap a few verses to guess, then scroll the chapter down and back up.
Tap **More** in the bottom tab bar, then close that menu.
Open **Psalm 23** and tap verse **Psalm 23:1**.
expected: **Play** closes the panel by itself. The bar sits just above the app's bottom bars. Its name, chances, **?**, latest message and **End game** are all fully visible and nothing runs off the side of the screen.
When scrolling makes the bottom bars slide down, the game bar moves down with them and stays fully visible; it comes back up when they do.
While the **More** menu is open the game bar is hidden, so it doesn't cover the menu. Closing the menu brings the bar back with the round still going.
Finding the verse reopens the panel by itself and shows the win screen with confetti and **You found it!**

tests.title: Everything is readable in dark mode
steps: Switch the app to dark mode in **Settings**.
Look at the start screen, the **Create a game** form (including a red error message), a round in play (panel and bar), and the win screen.
expected: All text, boxes, buttons and the greyed-out books and chapters are readable against the dark background. The bar and its buttons match the dark reader toolbar. Nothing shows as dark text on a dark box or a bright white box.

notCovered: Behaviour when loading, saving or deleting games fails on the server (the "Couldn't save that game" style messages). These are hard to trigger by hand and are covered by automated tests.

Reopening the panel in the split second while a save is still being written. This commit fixes a rare case where that could hide or later delete the new game. It's too quick to do by hand and is covered by automated tests.
Old saved games from before game names existed. None exist outside development.
Other languages: the game's text is only written in English so far.
Issue 1960 describes Phase 1 as local only (no saving). This PR also saves games to your account; these tests follow what the PR does.
